meeting_header:
Date: 2027-08-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:38 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Kapoor (Miramar Head of ML), Daniel Ruiz (Miramar Lead Platform Eng), Sofia Martins (Miramar CTO), Omar Haddad (Miramar Procurement)
summary: Weekly renewal/expansion check-in. Miramar is evaluating a 6-month contract extension with a committed reserved pool for peak trading hours plus APAC latency-zone activation. Main asks: predictable 99th p99 latency under 200ms for short chat queries, private VPC + KMS for keys, SOC2 audit docs, and clearer burst pricing. Redwood to run latency bench and deliver revised pricing/contract amendment. Next technical run week of Sept 6.
topics: APAC latency zones and region activation timeline
rollout and canary policy for model variants
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick agenda — pricing, latency zones, and the contract amendment.
[00:14] Priya Kapoor: Hey Ava, thanks. Um we just want to make sure we align on the goal: 6 month extension with an option to increase reserved capacity if the pilot hits volume. also apac region is a blocker for us.
[00:29] Liam Chen: (SE) yeah, hi Priya, hi Sofia. Quick clarifying question — when you say APAC block, do you mean full private vpc in ap-south-1 or just low-latency routing to hosted endpoints?
[00:42] Daniel Ruiz: We're leaning private VPC, our compliance folks prefer the private control plane for inference. that said, initial step could be routing to a nearby hosted edge to validate latency.
[00:55] Sofia Martins: Yep, and cost matters. we don't want to overcommit if traffic doesn't materialize.
[01:04] Ava Martinez: Understood. For the renewal we can propose a 6 month reserve with a burst pool and a region activation clause for APAC — that lets you enable ap-south-1 when ready.
[01:18] Omar Haddad: (Procurement) Quick from our side — will the contract include an SLA for p99 latency? that's important for exec sign off.
[01:27] Noah Patel: (CSM) Hey Omar, typically SLAs are for uptime/availability. p99 latency guarantees are tricky but we can commit to investigated SLOs and run benchmarked targets for your workload.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: Yeah we need a measurable target — specifically for short chat flows (<= 64 tokens) we want p95 < 120ms and p99 < 220ms if possible.
[01:53] Liam Chen: Noted — those numbers are tight but we can run targeted benches. question about model footprint: are you using the large ensemble or a single distilled model for prod?
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: We're currently on the large-2 ensemble for accuracy. may consider distilled for low-latency endpoints.
[02:13] Liam Chen: Okay that informs hardware and KV cache sizing. we'll run benches against both model variants.
[02:22] Daniel Ruiz: Also, encryption. We require KMS integration and customer-managed keys for any private deployment. is that supported?
[02:31] Ava Martinez: Yes, Redwood Private supports external KMS/HSM — we'll share the integration guide. but small caveat, for hosted endpoints there's an account-level KMS pattern; for Private you can bring your own key.
[02:46] Priya Kapoor: Good. please also include audit logs retention — we need 12 months.
[02:52] Noah Patel: We'll include retention config options.
[03:00] [00:03:00] Liam Chen: (starts to describe benchmark plan) So recommended approach: we spin up a dedicated test pool in eu-west-3 and ap-south-1, replicate sample traffic at peak hour tps, run 4 hour sustained test, collect p50/p95/p99, and KV cache hit rates. we can also test canary fallback to a quantized variant to measure delta.
[03:24] Priya Kapoor: That sounds good. can you also simulate cold starts? our traffic has bursty nightly behavior.
[03:31] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll do cold-start windows and warm cache windows.
[03:36] [00:03:36] Sofia Martins: On the pricing side, what changes if we add ap-south-1 region permanently — do we get a lower per-token rate if reserved?
[03:47] Ava Martinez: Adding a region to reserved commitment generally reduces incremental per-token costs for that region. we'll propose a tiered price: base reserved pool covers eu/us regions, add-on region discount for APAC when activated. I'll send the spreadsheet.
[04:00] Omar Haddad: How about burst overage pricing? we need predictability for budgeting.
[04:06] Ava Martinez: We'll provide explicit burst rates and a cap option — you can choose a soft cap or hard cap with auto-notify.
[04:13] [00:04:13] Daniel Ruiz: Any compatibility issues with our internal routing? we use Istio and corporate egress proxies.
[04:20] Liam Chen: No major issues, but for Private you'll want to map egress rules for the KMS calls. for hosted, we support IP allowlists and SSO. minor note: KV cache might require open egress to certain CDN endpoints. we'll include network hints.
[04:40] Priya Kapoor: About security — can you share SOC2 and pen test reports? the security team expects those before we sign.
[04:47] Noah Patel: Absolutely. I'll drop links to SOC2 attestation and last penetration test. (link posted) https://redwood.app/security/soc2-march2027.pdf
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: Great.
[05:02] [00:05:02] Liam Chen: One more technical note — we can enable prefix KV cache on the model to push down p99 by around 20-30% for short queries, but it increases memory footprint. that could push you toward dedicated capacity nodes.
[05:18] Sofia Martins: So tradeoff is cost vs latency. we need the bench results to decide.
[05:23] Ava Martinez: Exactly. our Optimize tooling will suggest quantization profiles and batch configs for each workload after we run the benches.
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: Ok, timeline wise — we need the pricing and docs by end of week for our legal review. can you do that?
[05:41] Ava Martinez: Yes, we'll send pricing spreadsheet and SOC2/KMS docs by Tuesday EOD.
[05:47] [00:05:47] Omar Haddad: procurement will review contract amendment draft; ideally we want a 6 month term with option to convert to annual if volume grows.
[05:56] Ava Martinez: We can put an option to convert with a lookback clause tied to sustained usage.
[06:03] Daniel Ruiz: For the bench, can VMware or our devops team get temporary admin access to the test cluster?
[06:10] Liam Chen: We'll provision a scoped test account with RBAC and ephemeral keys. no need for full admin.
[06:16] Priya Kapoor: Perfect.
[06:20] [00:06:20] Sofia Martins: On competitors, we've talked to CloudForge — their pricing is lower on token costs but they don't have the region routing/fallback Redwood described. also ModelServ offered a hard SLA but required a three-year commit, which we don't want.
[06:37] Ava Martinez: Good info — that helps position the tradeoffs.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: Also curious about rollback and canary — if a model version regresses, can traffic be auto-failed back to previous variant?
[06:49] Liam Chen: Yes, we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. note that fallback to a quantized variant might slightly change responses; we'll include acceptance criteria.
[06:59] [00:06:59] Noah Patel: Quick question from my side — is there any internal maintenance windows coming up in September that might affect provisioning?
[07:07] Priya Kapoor: We have a major release freeze Sept 10-14, but benching earlier that week is fine.
[07:13] Ava Martinez: We'll avoid that window.
[07:16] [00:07:16] (brief pause, 5s)
[07:22] Daniel Ruiz: Security asks: can we get the audit log schema? our SIEM needs certain fields.
[07:28] Noah Patel: I'll attach the schema to the follow-up doc.
[07:33] Priya Kapoor: Also legal will ask about data residency — if we enable APAC, logs must stay in-region.
[07:40] Liam Chen: For Private, logs can be routed to your in-region storage. for hosted, we can configure retention and region filters, but we'll need to confirm exact guarantees.
[07:52] [00:07:52] Ava Martinez: Okay quick recap before we wrap: Redwood to run latency bench for eu-west-3 and ap-south-1, share p50/p95/p99 and KV hit rates; Liam to post runbook and test account details; Ava to deliver pricing spreadsheet and contract amendment draft; Noah to attach SOC2 and audit log schema. Anything else?
[08:14] Priya Kapoor: Please include expected lead time to activate APAC region if we flip the switch.
[08:20] Ava Martinez: We'll include activation timeline — typically 10 business days for Private, 3-5 for hosted region enablement, subject to capacity.
[08:32] Omar Haddad: And confirm the burst cap option in the amendment.
[08:36] Ava Martinez: Noted.
[08:39] [00:08:39] (crosstalk) 
[08:45] Sofia Martins: last thing — do you have any reference customers running similar energy workflows in APAC?
[08:51] Liam Chen: We have a utilities customer in ap-south who did a region activation earlier this year — I'll anonymize and share a short note and benchmark snapshot.
[08:59] Priya Kapoor: thanks.
[09:02] [00:09:02] Ava Martinez: Great. We'll aim to have docs and pricing by next Tue, bench scheduled wk of Sept 6 pending your prompt set. Thanks everyone.
[09:14] Priya Kapoor: Thank you.
[09:16] (recording ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard terms (eg "KV cash" instead of KV cache; "Redwood Private" sometimes transcribed as "Redwoo Private"). Shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet link placeholder: https://redwood.app/decks/miramar-q3-playbook, SOC2 link posted earlier.
